pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is intonation? (1 mark)
   A. The rise and fall of the voice
   B. The number of words
   C. The spelling of words
   D. The size of letters

2. What does change mean in a shop? (1 mark)
   A. The clothes
   B. The weather
   C. Money given back after paying
   D. A journey

3. Which word shows a result? (1 mark)
   A. or
   B. but
   C. so
   D. and

4. Which answer is a full sentence for: Why did the pot tip over? (1 mark)
   A. Handle
   B. The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   C. Because
   D. Otieno

5. What should you do to check the punctuation in your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Cover it
   B. Tear it
   C. Write it again without looking
   D. Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses

6. What is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. A word that names a thing
   B. A word that shows position
   C. A word that joins sentences
   D. A short word that shows a sudden feeling

7. What does a picture story use? (1 mark)
   A. Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end
   B. Only numbers
   C. Only maps
   D. Only names

8. What does it mean to advocate for animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. To ignore them
   B. To harm animals
   C. To hide them
   D. To speak in support of caring for animals

9. A good storyteller (1 mark)
   A. forgets the ending
   B. practises and speaks clearly
   C. reads without looking
   D. whispers all the time

10. What should you do if you make a mistake in your exercise book? (1 mark)
   A. Scribble over it hard
   B. Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   C. Tear the page
   D. Blame a friend

11. Why is neat handwriting important? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the book heavier
   B. It helps the reader to understand the message
   C. It is only for teachers
   D. It makes the pencil last longer

12. In front of means (1 mark)
   A. behind it
   B. inside it
   C. before something and facing it
   D. under it

13. Why are stories important in communities? (1 mark)
   A. They teach values and keep history
   B. They hide the truth
   C. They waste time
   D. They cause trouble

14. What can wall charts of similes and metaphors help with? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking
   B. Sleeping
   C. Running
   D. Gallery walks and learning from each other

15. Which is a polite phrase for asking someone to explain again? (1 mark)
   A. You are silly
   B. Never mind
   C. Say it again now
   D. Pardon me, could you explain?

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Write a short speech of four sentences about caring for a goat. Use at least two prepositions. (5 marks)

17. Write one correct line of a dialogue with a speaker name and an interjection. (2 marks)

18. Give three rules for good turn taking. (3 marks)

19. Describe how you would play Simon says with your class and say what it teaches. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — The rise and fall of the voice
   Intonation is voice movement.

2. C — Money given back after paying
   Change is the money you get back.

3. C — so
   So shows a result.

4. B — The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   A full sentence has a subject and a verb and gives the reason.

5. D — Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses
   Reading aloud helps find where pauses and stops belong.

6. D — A short word that shows a sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotion.

7. A — Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end
   A picture story tells events with drawings.

8. D — To speak in support of caring for animals
   Advocating means speaking in support.

9. B — practises and speaks clearly
   Practice and clarity make a good teller.

10. B — Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   Neat correction keeps the page clean.

11. B — It helps the reader to understand the message
   A message is useful only if it can be read.

12. C — before something and facing it
   In front of shows the position ahead of something.

13. A — They teach values and keep history
   Stories teach and entertain.

14. D — Gallery walks and learning from each other
   Charts display the sayings for review.

15. D — Pardon me, could you explain?
   Pardon me and could you are polite.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two prepositions, for example Give the goat water beside the food. Build a shed behind the house. Do not put a heavy load on it. Call the veterinary doctor if it is sick.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for correct prepositions.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema: Wow! The sun is shining.
   Working / marking points: One mark for name with colon and one for an interjection.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wait for the speaker to finish, keep your turn short, do not always speak first, listen politely.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

19. (5 marks)
   Answer: One pupil is the leader. The leader gives instructions. Pupils obey only when the leader says Simon says. Those who obey a wrong instruction are out. The game teaches careful listening.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the leader, one for the rule, one for what happens when a player breaks the rule, and two marks for explaining what it teaches.
